units: pixels (frame pixel coordinates, x right, y down) and seconds; no metric scale is assumed
summary: Indoor basketball court, camera roughly facing the baseline wall and hoop. A person (cap, beige top, olive cargo pants, white sneakers; face blurred) stands left of the hoop holding a basketball at face level, dips, jumps and releases a one-handed/two-handed jump shot at frame ~54. The ball flies up and to the right, reaches its apex at frame 71 in front of the backboard glass (above rim height), misses the rim entirely (no contact with rim or board), falls to the floor right of the lane and bounces three times (floor contacts frames 97, 135, 164, a 4th contact at the very end ~187) while drifting right. The person lands (frame ~63), stands, then walks to the right from about frame 90-105 to the end.

camera.drift_vs_frame0: image of a static point shifts by up to dx = -19 px, dy = -29 px and rotates up to +1.05 deg (roll) by the last frame; scale change < 0.6 %
camera.per_frame_file: tracks/camera_shift.csv (similarity transform frame-0 -> frame-i: scale, roll, shift of image centre)
camera.compensated_coordinates: track columns *_bgfixed_px are positions mapped back to frame-0 background coordinates (use these for motion)

perspective.note: Camera height ~ eye level, optical axis roughly perpendicular to the baseline wall. Floor recedes upward. The person and ball move mostly parallel to the image plane but the shot also has a depth component (ball apparent diameter 48-49 px in the hands, ~43 px near the apex/hoop, 46-48 px after the bounces).

objects.reference_point: visible centre of the ball (x = centre of horizontal extent, y = row of maximum width, robust to vertical motion blur)
objects.notes: Held in the hands frames 0-53 (partly covered by fingers; centre still reliable to ~3 px). Mask degraded frames 73-77 (ball overlaps the black pole/'3' logo behind the glass) and at floor contacts (reflection merges): flagged in occluded_or_degraded.

objects.notes: Feet stand on a glossy floor with a strong mirror reflection; the box bottom is the sole/floor contact row read on keyframes and interpolated (+-4 px). Airborne frames 55-62 use the lowest visible foot.

ball release (first frame clearly free of the fingers)

ball 4th floor contact at/after the last frame (descending at 187)
